# Anthropic Managed Agents — self-hosted sandboxes + security model (literal)
# Captured 2026-10-11 from
#   https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes
#   https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes-security

CREATE: POST /v1/environments  {"name":"...","config":{"type":"self_hosted"}}
  beta header: managed-agents-2026-04-01
  CLI: ant apply environment.yaml   (schema platform.claude.com/schemas/ant/beta/environment.json)

MODEL: the environment is a WORK QUEUE. Anthropic keeps orchestration; the customer runs an
ENVIRONMENT WORKER that claims work items, downloads the agent's skills + the session's memory
stores, executes each tool call locally, and posts results back. Tool inputs AND OUTPUTS still
flow to Anthropic's control plane.

NEW CREDENTIAL TYPES:
  ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY  (sk-ant-oat01-...)  authenticates the worker to its queue.
      CONSOLE-ONLY issuance, even for an API-created environment.
      Scoped to ONE environment's work queue. Revocation validated on every request.
  per-work-item `secret`  — the ONLY credential the memory-store endpoints accept
      (they reject the environment key). Must not be logged or shared across sandboxes.

CLAUDE PLATFORM ON AWS: worker authenticates with IAM SigV4 (or a Console-generated AWS API key),
  managed policy `AnthropicSelfHostedEnvironmentAccess`. Claude Console environment keys DO NOT
  work against that endpoint.

WORKER: `ant beta:worker poll --workdir /workspace` (workdir defaults to cwd; system default
  /workspace). Needs /bin/bash at that exact path and outbound HTTPS only.
  Stats: `ant beta:environments:work stats --environment-id ...` -> workers_polling
  If no worker is connected the session STAYS QUEUED rather than failing.

SESSION RESOURCES: memory_store ONLY. A `file` or `github_repository` resource => 400
  "Environment env_... is a self-hosted environment. `resources` are not supported with
   self-hosted environments." Same rule applies to scheduled deployments.

VENDOR WORKER BUILDS: AWS Lambda MicroVMs, Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Fly.io,
  GKE Agent Sandbox, Modal, Namespace, Superserve, Vercel.

INDEPENDENT OF MCP TUNNELS (self-hosting = where code runs; tunnels = how Anthropic reaches
  private MCP servers). Either combination is valid.

SECURITY MODEL — customer owns:
  sandbox image quality + runtime hardening (Anthropic does NOT inspect or verify the image)
  network egress controls (customer VPC/firewall only)
  environment service key storage + rotation
  isolating untrusted workloads (one workspace+environment per trust boundary)
  per-session `secret` handling
  tool-execution blast radius
  log retention + session content
  memory store local copies under /mnt/memory/

*** read_only MEMORY STORES: "protected from upload, not from local modification."
    worker write/edit tools refuse; memory-store endpoints reject writes with the session secret;
    BUT bash, custom tools and sandbox-served MCP servers run with the worker's permissions and
    CAN rewrite the local copy. Later tool calls in that session read the changed copy.
    Documented mitigation: disable bash for that agent + give no filesystem-writing custom tool.
*** A worker that exits WITHOUT running teardown LEAVES THE MEMORY COPY ON DISK.

"What Anthropic cannot do for you": know that your key leaked; verify your worker build
  (supply-chain compromise in the image is NOT detectable from the control plane); isolate tools
  inside your sandbox; enforce data retention in your environment ("once session content reaches
  your worker, it is outside Anthropic's data lifecycle controls").
